title: Homing projectile
subtitle: Build a readable homing projectile with a reachable response and a useful recovery.
summary: A projectile adjusts its heading toward the player after launch.
overview: A projectile adjusts its heading toward the player after launch, creating a moving pursuit problem instead of a single predicted line.
learning: Tune the signal, commitment, geometry, response, and recovery of a homing projectile as one rule.

demo.title: Test the homing projectile
phaseDescriptions: Identify lock-on and tracking strength through a marker, curved trail, or turning pose before the projectile reaches close range.
Allow sharp direction changes, cover, interception, outrunning, or redirection according to the game’s verbs, and establish when tracking stops.
Tracking ends at a communicated cutoff and the projectile expires or travels straight, ensuring the pursuit creates a finite response window.

steps.title: Can the player read the complete rule?
steps.body: Identify lock-on and tracking strength through a marker, curved trail, or turning pose before the projectile reaches close range.

steps.title: Is the intended response reachable?
steps.body: Allow sharp direction changes, cover, interception, outrunning, or redirection according to the game’s verbs, and establish when tracking stops.

steps.title: Does recovery create a useful outcome?
steps.body: Tracking ends at a communicated cutoff and the projectile expires or travels straight, ensuring the pursuit creates a finite response window.

mistakes.title: Perfect turning with no lifetime or cutoff forces a specific exploit instead of supporting readable movement
mistakes.body: Perfect turning with no lifetime or cutoff forces a specific exploit instead of supporting readable movement.

mistakes.title: The cue and active geometry disagree
mistakes.body: If the visible homing projectile cue promises a different area or timing, the player cannot carry the learned rule into the next cycle.

designNotes.title: Tune the complete rule
designNotes.body: Tune speed, turn rate, tracking delay, lifetime, and collision size together; a slower projectile can still be inescapable with unlimited turning.

designNotes.title: Escalate one variable at a time
designNotes.body: Combine weak homing with obstacles or stagger several lock times rather than simply raising turn rate to perfect tracking.

designNotes.title: Prove the recovery
designNotes.body: Tracking ends at a communicated cutoff and the projectile expires or travels straight, ensuring the pursuit creates a finite response window.

story.title: What the mechanic communicates
story.body: A projectile adjusts its heading toward the player after launch, creating a moving pursuit problem instead of a single predicted line. The encounter uses that rule as a short promise: a visible signal, a committed action, and a result the player can verify.

adaptation.title: Adapt it to the player verbs
adaptation.body: Allow sharp direction changes, cover, interception, outrunning, or redirection according to the game’s verbs, and establish when tracking stops. Tune speed, turn rate, tracking delay, lifetime, and collision size together; a slower projectile can still be inescapable with unlimited turning.

distinction.title: Keep the mechanic distinct
distinction.body: Perfect turning with no lifetime or cutoff forces a specific exploit instead of supporting readable movement. Do not hide that distinction behind extra effects or tracking that the announced rule does not contain.

lensNotes.body: The signal must reveal the relevant timing and geometry before commitment.
After commitment, the rule stops changing in ways the signal did not announce.
Preparation, action, and recovery create a legible cycle of pressure and release.
The response uses an ordinary supported verb and produces an observable result.

examples.body: Absolute Radiance demonstrates homing projectile in a 2D encounter. Identify lock-on and tracking strength through a marker, curved trail, or turning pose before the projectile reaches close range.
